newsitem.title: GERMANY: Russia 96 aluminium exports seen at 2.0-2.3 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Russia 96 aluminium exports seen at 2.0-2.3 mln T.

text.p: Russian aluminium exports to the western world were estimated at between two and 2.3 million tonnes this year, German aluminium industry association GDA said at a press conference on Tuesday.

GDA general secretary Christian Wellner, who gave the figure in response to questions, said, "We assume this figure will remain steady in the next few years, as long as the region fails to build up its own markets."
He did not provide comparative figures.
His remark was in contrast to recent analysts' forecasts.

Major aluminium player Transworld sees exports of 1.8 to 1.9 million tonnes in 1996. Adam Rowley of Macquarie Bank Group and Alan Williamson of Bain & Co in a Sept 9 interview said they envisaged falling exports from Russia in the first half of 1997.

But the 2.0-2.3 million would not weigh down western European prices as during the unprecedented influx of Russian material in the early 1990s because markets had grown used to absorbing this tonnage, Wellner said.
"This volume is now established...there is no excess volume," Wellner said.
Apart from primary metal, Russia also exported extrusions, where sales were insignificant, but rolled products exports out of Russia had risen this year.

GDA president Walter Hueck said while there was still an idle capacity reserve of one million tonnes of global primary output as a result of voluntary producer cuts, this would quickly come on stream if demand picked up.
"If the automotive sector recovered, that million (tonnes) would be absorbed very quickly," Hueck said.
"Unfortunately, ordering by carmakers is always the result of many decentralised decisions." --Vera Eckert, Duesseldorf newsroom, +49-211-3882-243
